Subject: Private deployment — next steps on license boundary and evidence

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team followed up with a short list of requirements for an on-prem / VPC deployment. The two items that are blocking procurement are:

- Clarify the license scope: whether Redwood grants a perpetual runtime license to run the model binaries in our environment or a time-limited service license tied to a subscription.
- Evidence delivery / custody: our auditors want a concrete path for evidence (logs, audit trail, attestation) and an option similar to an escrow for model custody in the event of contract termination.

I've attached the HealthSync_Audit_Request_20260618.pdf with specifics. Can Redwood share a proposed addendum and a suggested evidence handling flow so our legal and cloud teams can review? Tim (copied) is our external counsel and will coordinate redlines.

Appreciate a quick turnaround—our board is reviewing the procurement by the end of the month.

Best,
Sarah Patel
Head of Infrastructure
HealthSync, Inc.

Immediate plan from Redwood:
1) We will produce a short addendum (MSA addendum + exemplar order form paragraph) that:
   - Defines license grant as a "runtime license" tied to an active subscription for the service or the dedicated instance — not a transfer of IP.
   - Includes a limited post-termination execution window (e.g., 30–90 days) for a temporary custody period if you need to export models or logs.
2) Evidence flow proposal: we will propose a three-tier model — online audit portal + periodic export package + escrow-like custody option (for exceptional termination scenarios).
3) Deliverables: draft addendum (docx), evidence inventory template (csv), and a short FAQ for auditors.

Vanessa — quick notes on redline posture from product/legal side. I'm putting bullet-level text we can drop into the addendum:

- License scope: "Customer is granted a non-exclusive, non-transferable runtime license to execute Redwood-provided model artifacts and runtime components within Customer's designated environment for the duration of the Order Form subscription. No assignment of model IP or source code is conveyed."

- Post-termination custody window: "Upon expiry/termination, Customer has 45 days to export runtime artifacts and KV caches; Redwood will provide an export package containing logs and metadata necessary for verification."

- Evidence delivery: "Redwood will provide monthly audit packages via a secure SFTP link and offer a one-time full export on reasonable request. For escalations, Redwood can arrange a custodial handoff to a mutually-agreed third-party escrow agent; costs borne by Customer unless otherwise agreed."

- Data retention / access controls: include an explicit list of audit logs provided and redaction obligations.

I'll draft language and attach it to the addendum docx. Jasmine, can you confirm the operational runbook steps for generating the export packages (SFTP vs signed transfer)?

Notes from ops side — draft runbook points: 

- Export mechanics: we support AES-256 archive exports delivered over SFTP or to a customer-supplied cloud bucket (preferably temporary pre-signed URL). Exports include:
  * access_logs.json (ingestion + inference events)
  * kv_cache_manifest.txt (key IDs + ranges)
  * model_manifest.json (model name, version, quantization)
  * operational_metrics.csv

- SLA for exports: standard turnaround 5 business days for scheduled monthly exports; expedited 48–72 hours for termination-triggered full export (subject to queueing).

- Escrow agent: we have a small set of third-party providers we've used for similar custody handoffs — will attach vendor list and estimated fees.

- Security: all exports are encrypted in transit and at rest; Redwood will provide a signed hash manifest for verification.

Neha — any legal redlines on the timeframe or the wording about costs?

Jasmine
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

All — quick legal guidance to keep in the addendum: 

1) Avoid the term "perpetual" for runtime rights. Make the grant explicit that it is contingent on a live Order Form and not a transfer of IP.
2) Make custody/escrow optional and subject to a separate fee and SLA. We should offer the operational details (runbook) but avoid insuring custody costs unless Customer accepts.
3) For export timing, 45 days is okay but include language that Redwood may require a short extension if export size or legal hold exists; include an escalation path to Redwood legal for exceptions.
4) Ensure we include a narrow indemnity carve-out for misuse of exported model artifacts (e.g., if Customer redistributes models).

I'll review the draft addendum and mark final redlines. Karthik — please include the indemnity bullet.

Neha Kapoor

Sarah / Tim — attaching Redwood_Private_Addendum_v1.docx which incorporates the internal bullets above, plus the evidence_inventory_template.csv. Highlights:

- License: runtime license tied to Order Form; no IP transfer.
- Post-termination export: 45-day standard window, with a documented extension process.
- Evidence exports: monthly packages via SFTP or customer bucket; expedited full export on termination.
- Custodial escrow: optional, third-party agent, costs to customer unless agreed otherwise.
- Indemnity: limited carve for redistribution of model artifacts.

Next steps I propose:
1) Tim / HealthSync: please review and send redlines into the docx.
2) If you want a sandbox export to validate the format, Jasmine can schedule a sample export next week.
3) We'll list escrow agent options and ballpark fees in a short appendix.

Tim — can you confirm whether HealthSync's legal wants escrow as a pre-condition or a fallback option? That will change the commercial ask.

Thanks — aiming to have a mutually-agreeable addendum and a one-page evidence playbook by end of next week.
